newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN urges E. Europe to scrap investment obstacles.
newsitem.headline: ABN urges E. Europe to scrap investment obstacles.

text.p: ABN AMRO Bank chairman Jan Kalff urged Eastern European countries on Thursday to remove obstacles to private foreign investment in their infrastructure.
Kalff said foreign investment was sorely needed in sectors such as telecommunications, power generation and transport if the region was to attain the high growth levels forecast for it.
But potential foreign investment in infrastructure projects was blocked by unfavourable conditions, Kalff told a business conference on Central and Eastern Europe in The Hague.
"It is still deterred by the perceived high risk of the business environment, by the chaotic legal, regulatory and procedural impediments encountered all too frequently," he said.
Unless this situation was redressed Eastern Europe would continue to lose out to Asia and Latin America which continued to attract a far larger share of investment inflows, he said.
Kalff urged countries in the region to create a level playing field in which all investors, both foreign and domestic were treated equally.
He said they should also accelerate improvements in their banking systems, step up the pace of bank privatisations and develop working capital markets and pension fund systems.
